## Interpretation (analyst reading, not measured)

All 24 observations date from one reading of the owner's Saved collections on 2026-10-09 (captions and alt text only; no reels watched; no engagement numbers). So this is a reading of what the owner chose to save, not of what performed. Four patterns recur:

- **Operator-authority carousels** (ins_2026-10-09_01, _02, _11, _13, _14, _19): a hook that names a mistake or a shift, then lesson slides, then a save ask. They may work because gym owners and trainers follow accounts that make them feel competent, and a carousel rewards saving. For FitFlex this is the run_gym and grow_business pillars; the week-1 A and B carousels and the week-3 record already use this structure.
- **Comment-keyword funnels** (ins_2026-10-09_05, _16, _20, _24): the ask converts a passive viewer into a DM and a lead. It may work because it lowers the step from "interested" to "in contact". For FitFlex it only works once someone answers the comments (manual now, comment-to-DM later), so the first posts should expect a handful of comments, not a funnel.
- **Local voice, short Swahili-first captions, price on screen** (ins_2026-10-09_17, _18, _22): the Tanzanian accounts in the set keep captions to a line or two and put the concrete fact (price, place) on the image. It may work because the audience scans in Swahili on a phone. For FitFlex this argues for shorter captions than the week-1 drafts and for the marketplace pillar once real vendor prices exist.
- **Community and build-in-public** (ins_2026-10-09_03, _06, _09, _10, _12): event recaps, openings, construction updates, "the gym is a culture" framing. It may work because it gives followers a reason to return between offers. For FitFlex this is the community pillar and depends on partner gyms agreeing to be featured.

These are interpretations of a biased sample. Nothing above has been measured on the FitFlex account, which has published nothing yet.

## Proposed experiments (no guaranteed outcomes)

1. **Caption length.** Hypothesis: a one-line Swahili-first caption gets more saves per reach than the three-line week-1 style. Create two member carousels that differ only in caption length. Metric: saves per 100 reach. Judge after at least 3 posts per arm.
2. **Hook type on owner carousels.** Hypothesis: a data-style hook ("the number you don't track") beats a contrarian hook for saves among owners. Two run_gym carousels, same structure, different slide 1. Metric: saves. At least 3 per arm.
3. **Keyword CTA vs no CTA.** Hypothesis: a keyword ask increases comments but not reach. Pair each keyword post with a non-keyword twin of the same pillar. Metrics: comments and reach. At least 3 pairs.
4. **Posting day.** Metricool's best-time data is all zeros today (no history). After 8 posts, read `getBestTimeToPostByNetwork` again before moving slots.

None of these promises an outcome; each ends with a note in `learnings.md` whether or not the hypothesis held.

## Limitations

- Single observation date (2026-10-09), single source (the owner's Saved collections), first ~12 posts per collection only.
- No engagement metrics on any record; reels not watched; no post URLs captured (the swipe file recorded accounts and captions, not links). Future sweeps capture the URL per post.
- No observations for clubs and communities, real estate, Kenya or Uganda; the owner still needs to create those collections.
- Nothing has been measured on the FitFlex account; `learnings.md` reports zero published posts.
- The categories reflect the owner's interests (operator view, supply side) more than the member audience.
